static_traits.name: An Li
static_traits.educational_background: Has taken systematic music lessons since age 5
static_traits.family_status: Living alone; best friend is in a band
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with best friend tense due to Anxiety; usually seeks help from them but finds it hard to talk about self-blame and Anxiety
static_traits.medical_history: Without significant physical illness; without similar prior psychological problems or treatment history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe automatic thoughts and emotions specifically; cooperative, Positive attitude; habitually using self-blaming phrasings, easily focusing on negative evaluations

basic_info.main_problem: I keep feeling pressured and responsible for the quality of the songs I create, leading to self-blame and Anxiety.
basic_info.core_demands: The overwhelming self-blame and Anxiety have started affecting my creativity and overall enjoyment of music; this is why I am seeking counseling now.
growth_experiences: Since age 5 has received systematic music training and courses, developing in the music field for a long time; this specialized training constitutes the basis of the client's self-identity and career path.

Increased stress after making music a career, markedly intensified in the past year; In a live performance, one song received negative feedback became a clear turning point, triggering Persistent self-doubt and Anxiety, manifesting as strong unease before creating and performing, Sleep disturbed, attention affected.

core_beliefs: As long as the work is not good enough, It is all my fault
I am not talented enough / not good enough
Failure means I am not suited for music (failure = total negation)

special_situations.event: In a live performance, one song received negative feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a work receives negative evaluation, it proves I am not talented enough, not suited for music
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly seeking others' feedback and comparing with mature Musicians, Reinforcement of self-criticism to 'avoid failing again'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They no longer take me seriously, I am not suited for music.

special_situations.event: In the process of creating new songs
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a work does not reach very high standards, it is a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly revising and Self-denial, increasing self-pressure to force perfection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This song is not good enough, I failed again.

special_situations.event: Imagining the audience's reaction before performing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make mistakes or my work is Average, the audience will hate me, and I will disappoint everyone
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-rehearsing worst-case scenarios, excessive tension and Self-monitoring to avoid mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The audience will hate this song, find it boring, I will disappoint everyone.

special_situations.event: Receives feedback that is mainly positive but includes a small amount of negative opinion
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative comments are more real and more representative of the work's overall level
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring positive information, only fixating on negative reviews and thinking repeatedly
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those negative evaluations show that my work is overall poor.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and taken seriously as a talented Musician, with works liked and affirmed
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and negation, worrying about not being taken seriously, being belittled or excluded
defense_goal: Gains a sense of control and preempts external blame by taking all responsibility onto self
Maintaining perfect standards to avoid criticism
Reducing exposure of vulnerability in relationships, lowering help-seeking to avoid appearing 'not good enough'

object_relations.self_representation: Not talented enough, A person who easily disappoints others
object_relations.object_representation: A harsh judge/picky audience or authority

object_relations.self_representation: A person who finds it hard to express vulnerability and worries about troubling others
object_relations.object_representation: Friends who may not understand or may be burdened by me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about or recalling negative feedback, works being criticized or not liked
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing others' constructive feedback as a total negation of self-worth
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blaming and apologetic language, repeatedly emphasizing 'It is all my fault', ignoring context and multiple causes.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Before a performance or in sessions, when discussing potential audience reactions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing inner Self-doubt and harsh judgment to the audience, assuming others will belittle oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using phrasings like 'they will hate me / think I am not good', fixating on speculating about others' minds, avoiding exploring one's true needs and boundaries.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to distinguish facts from evaluations, or Guided to notice positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Automatically internalizes external high standards and others' evaluations as absolute rules that must be followed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using rule-based language like 'I must/should......', insisting on perfect standards, hard to accept gray areas and flexibility.

manifestations: Attributes all responsibility for the work's quality to oneself, experiencing a heavy inner 'must' and responsibility
Fearing that making mistakes equals being unsuited for music
Living alone, main support source is the best friend in the band
Difficulty discussing self-blame and Anxiety with friends
Self-blame and Anxiety beginning to erode enjoyment of music and creativity

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly describing problems in a self-blaming way in sessions ('It is all my fault'), harsh self-evaluation
Cautious when expressing, worried about disappointing others

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assuming in sessions that the audience will hate the songs or find them boring, attributing inner Self-doubt to others' negative evaluations

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizing external standards like 'if the work is not good it is my fault' as absolute rules, hard to flexibly adjust

exception_events.target_problem: When creating new songs or before performing, An Li is usually trapped by self-blame and Anxiety, experiencing strong Self-doubt, disrupted sleep, and impaired performance and focus.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In several past performances, despite great worry beforehand, the performances went well on the day, overall exceeding Anticipation.
exception_events.reason: Different understanding/approach: reminding oneself of the love for music during the performance, and recalling past successes, thus buffering the intensity of Self-doubt.

positive_force: Love of music and long-term systematic training (since age 5)
Had Good performance experiences before, usable as confidence and evidence resources
Willing to try new strategies (such as recording positive feedback and successful experiences), open to change
Has potential social support (best friend is in the band)
negative_force: Cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, black-and-white, personalization are prominent
Over-focusing on negative evaluations and ignoring positive information, repeatedly comparing with mature Musicians
By taking all responsibility onto oneself to gain a sense of control, leading to persistent self-blame
Sleep disturbance and impaired attention, forming an Anxiety--function-impairment vicious cycle
Difficulty expressing vulnerability in relationships, support resources not yet fully utilized

target_behavior.behavior: High Anxiety and self-blame before creating and performing (with repeated Self-denial speech)
antecedent: Starting to write a new song
Thinking about possible negative feedback or mistakes
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic interpretation of failure and the core belief 'if the work is not good It is all my fault'; inferiority and perfectionistic standards from comparing with mature Musicians.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential failure and external judgment, gaining temporary control and safety through self-blame
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in creativity, stage Performance affected, disrupted sleep and Decreased attention, further aggravating Anxiety

target_behavior.behavior: Selectively focuses on negative feedback and ruminates repeatedly
antecedent: Receiving others' feedback on the work or performance
Reviewing situations where performances and works were judged
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive patterns of mental filtering and negating positive information; Introjecting harsh external standards as self-evaluation yardsticks.
target_behavior.function: Maintains self-vigilance to 'avoid making mistakes again', trying to prevent risks through self-criticism
target_behavior.consequence: Self-doubt deepened, Interpersonal tension (relationship with best friend affected), Anxiety maintained
